_comment: "When this attacks draw a card, then discard a random card. If a card with 6 or more {p} is discarded this way, destroy a random item in the arena." Was on test_invented_refs.py's KNOWN_UNFIXED with the diagnosis 'destroy a RANDOM item in the arena -- object targets prompt, never roll': the DESTROY_REF read ref 'ITEM', a name nothing sets, so the destroy silently did nothing and the whole payoff clause was dead. SELECT_FROM_ZONE now takes random:true and reaches the arena zones, so the item is PICKED rather than prompted -- prompting would hand the controller a choice the card explicitly denies them. player:ANY because 'the arena' is the shared play area, not just your own items; the selection fans out over both players' item zones. The random pick uses the module rng, the same source effect_discard's random discard already uses, so a seeded game stays reproducible. The gate is DISCARDED_CARD_POWER_GTE, which reads what the discard actually took rather than what was merely in hand, and CONDITIONAL scopes the destroy to it so 'if a card with 6 or more {p} is discarded this way' is real. Nothing is stored when no item qualifies, so DESTROY_REF finds no target and does nothing rather than erroring.
